en: The Great Dhāraṇī of the Sovereign of Great Spells, the Universal Radiance,
Pure and Blazing Wish-Fulfilling Jewel Seal of the Heart, the Unconquerable One,
Volume One.

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Da Xingshan Monastery, who holds the rank of Kaifu Yitong Sansi, Teci, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, Duke of Su with a fief of three thousand households, recipient of the purple robe, posthumously honored as Minister of Works, and titled Dajian (Great Mirror) with the posthumous epithet Zheng (Correct), and bearing the name Dayangzhi (Great Vast Wisdom). By Imperial Decree. Chapter One: The Introduction. Thus have I heard.
At one time, the Bhagavān was dwelling in the pavilion atop the Great Vajra Sumeru Peak,
abiding in the Great Vajra Samādhi.
The kalpa-trees were adorned with great vajras;
they shone with the light of precious lotuses in the great vajra pond,
and the ground was strewn with vajra-sand.
Within the Great Vajra Empowerment,
in the Vajra Maṇḍala and the palace of Śakra, Lord of the Devas,
there was a great vajra lion throne adorned with hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of ornaments.
This is the locus of the supernatural power of preaching the Dharma.
It is sustained by the sovereign spiritual power (*adhiṣṭhāna*) of all Tathāgatas.
One enters into the equality of all phenomena and gives rise to the wisdom of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*).
He was accompanied by a multitude of eighty-four koṭi-nayuta bodhisattvas,
all of whom were in their final birth before buddhahood (ekajātipratibaddha) and had attained non-retrogression from anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
They all attained great power.
They all manifested the buddha-field supernormal powers of the Great Vajra Liberation Samādhi,
entering the mental activities of all sentient beings in a single kṣaṇa.
They have accomplished various kinds of exquisite, vast, and profound skillful expositions of all dharmas;
their eloquence is unimpeded, they have attained great supernormal powers,
and they are fully able to make offerings to the Tathāgatas in immeasurable Buddha-worlds.
The mastery of the samādhi of liberation through the ocean-like clouds of great offerings,
the uncommon factors of enlightenment, the branches of the path, all the stages, and the perfections;
skillfulness in the four means of attraction, compassion, joy, and equanimity, and the power of purification within the continuity of the mind.
Their names were:
the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajragarbha and the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajranetra.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrakāya,
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajramati,
and the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi.
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrasaṃghaṭṭana,
the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajranārāyaṇa,
and the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajravikrīḍita.
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrasambhava,
the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajracūḍa,
and the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrasūkṣma.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajradhvaja was present,
together with a host of such leading Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas,
as well as a great assembly of Śrāvakas, all of whom were Great Arhats.
Having severed the fetters of existence and exhausted all outflows,
they attain wholesome and right knowledge and are well-liberated in mind;
they are fully able to manifest inconceivable supernormal powers and the superknowledge of psychic travel, sporting therein with ease.
They all attained great power in their vision of non-attachment;
free from all defilements, they incinerated the seeds of habitual tendencies.
Their names were the Venerable Śāriputra, and so forth.
The Venerable Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra,
the Venerable Kapphiṇa,
and the Venerable Subhūti.
The Venerable Kāśyapa,
the Venerable Mahākāśyapa,
and the Venerable Uruvilvākāśyapa.
He was accompanied by such a host of eminent great śrāvakas as these.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by the son of the Great Lord (Maheśvara) as his chief,
together with an immeasurable, boundless, unspeakable, and incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) multitude of devaputras from the Pure Abodes (*śuddhāvāsa*).
Furthermore, there was Mahābrahmā, the lord of the Sahā world, acting as the leader,
together with the sons of the gods of the Brahma assembly;
and there were also the sons of the gods of Suyāma, Nirmāṇarati, and Paranirmitavaśavartin.
Śakra, the Lord of Devas, was also present, accompanied by his retinue of various devaputras.
Furthermore, there were the asura kings Vemacitrin and Mālin.
[He] caused the Asura King Pramoda,
the Asura King Prabhāsa,
and the Asura King Rāhu to rejoice.
Thus, the preeminent Asura King was accompanied by an immeasurable and boundless host of Asura Kings as his retinue;
furthermore, there was the Naga King Sāgara.
The nāga king Takṣaka,
the nāga king Vāsuki, the nāga king Śaṅkhapāla,
and the nāga king Karkoṭaka.
The Nāga King Padma,
the Nāga King Mahāpadma,
and other such preeminent nāga kings.
He was accompanied by an immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) multitude of nāga kings.
Furthermore, there was the kinnara king Druma,
together with an immeasurable retinue of kinnara kings.
Furthermore, there was the vidyādhara king Sarvārthasiddha,
accompanied by an immeasurable retinue of vidyādhara kings;
and also the gandharva king Pañcaśikha.
Together with an immeasurable retinue of gandharva kings;
furthermore, there was the king of the kinnaras,
Suvarṇa-rajata-kinnara, together with an immeasurable retinue of kinnara kings.
Furthermore, there are the yakṣa king Bahudhāraṇī,
the yakṣa king Ratnacitta,
and the yakṣa king Pūrṇacitta.
The yakṣa king Pañcika was present together with an immeasurable and boundless retinue of yakṣa kings,
as well as Hārītī.
Accompanied by his five hundred sons as his retinue, he was further joined by the seven World-Protecting Mother Goddesses,
the seven Great Rākṣasī Mothers,
and the seven Celestial Seers who roam through space.
The deities of the nine planets,
the earth deities of the cardinal and intermediate directions,
and the goddess Sarasvatī.
Accompanied by his retinue,
there were also obstacle-creating Vināyakas and Bhūtas.
The bhūtas are all possessed of great majesty and power,
each accompanied by their own retinues.
Furthermore, there were all the kings of mountains,
all the kings of oceans,
as well as the World-Protectors, the King of Waters, and Varuṇa.
Also present were Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the Heavenly King of the East; Virūḍhaka, the Heavenly King of the South;
Virūpākṣa, the Heavenly King of the West; the Rākṣasa Lord Daṇḍapāṇi; the Seven Wind Deities; and Īśāna together with his consort.
Together with a retinue of a thousand koṭis of nayutas,
there was also the god Nārāyaṇa together with his retinue.
Furthermore, there are the Nata-karnaka, the Ruhaka,
and the Mahā-gaṇapati.
The Vighna-kings such as Mījugraka and others were accompanied by an immeasurable and boundless retinue of vighnas. Furthermore,
there were sixty kings who roam through various castles and fortresses, each accompanied by their own retinues.
Furthermore, there were four sisters who were goddesses,
together with their brother, as their retinue;
there was also the goddess Vajraśaṅkarī.
He was accompanied by a retinue of sixty-four vajra-daughters,
as well as the youth Vajrasena and the youth Somahu.
The youth Mūrdhagata was accompanied by an immeasurable retinue of the Vajra clans,
as well as those who possessed pure faith in the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha.
Devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas,
kiṃnaras, mahoragas, bhūtas,
and piśācas.
Aprasama-ra | Ummānasatya-sa | Hiri-ka |
Uṣadharaka, along with the Sun and Moon Devas— the deities of dawn, midday, evening, midnight, and all times—
accompanied by immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) retinues.
Thereupon, the World-Honored One, having successfully turned the Wheel of Dharma and completed his Buddha-work,
reached the ultimate perfection of merit and wisdom,
and fully embraced the Great Bodhi of omniscience.
They attain the blazing stage of the pāramitās;
they adorn the dharma-body with the thirty-two marks of a great man,
and they adorn all its limbs with the eighty-four secondary characteristics.
The crown-mark of all sentient beings has nothing upon which to gaze;
it transcends and surpasses all Māras and penetrates the knowledge of all-knowledge.
He is fully endowed with the five eyes;
he has accomplished all marks;
he has accomplished the knowledge of all-knowing wisdom.
Accomplishing all Buddha-dharmas,
crushing all māras and heterodox arguments,
his lofty and eminent fame resounds as the great heroic lion’s roar.
He destroys the darkness of ignorance by means of the perfections of generosity,

ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, wisdom, skillful means, aspiration, power, and knowledge, as well as difficult practices and ascetic austerities accumulated over immeasurable, boundless, incalculable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of kalpas.
He attained the adornment of the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty-four secondary characteristics;
his body sat upon a lion throne within the treasury of a great jewel, vajra, and lotus.
The seat was adorned with a net of immeasurable vajra-jewels, which,
when stirred by a gentle breeze, produced sublime sounds;
it was established through the power of the immeasurable vajra-realm’s divine feet.
Adorned with immeasurable vajra-jewels,
he emits red pearls from his makara mouth and then draws them back into his mouth again.
The filaments of the lotus were adorned with immeasurable jewels:
amber and great amber,
sapphire and great sapphire.
Puṣpalaṅka was adorned with a network of radiant light, universally magnificent and beautiful;
it featured a canopy adorned with immeasurable vajra-jewels, supported by handles made of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of kalpa-trees.
Adorned with a majestic canopy of shade,
his seat was vast and expansive like Mount Sumeru,
resembling a mountain of gold.
Adorned with the splendor of auspicious, blazing radiance,
it outshines a thousand suns;
its ground is perfectly round, like the pure moon.
May all sentient beings find deep delight in beholding the Dharma of the Tathāgata,
which is like a great kalpa-tree in full bloom;
may the sublime Dharma he proclaims be virtuous in its beginning, middle, and end.
Its meaning is profound and far-reaching; its phrasing is skillful and elegant.
It is pure, pristine, and unadulterated.
At that time, from the ūrṇā-kośa on the crown of his head, the World-Honored One—
He emitted a great radiance, the light of which was named "The Net of Light Manifesting All Tathāgatas.
By means of this radiance,
he universally illumined the trichiliocosm and even as many Buddha-worlds as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River.
In that world, all the Tathāgatas were preaching the Dharma upon lion thrones adorned with immeasurable jewels within the Great Adorned Pavilion,
together with all the bodhisattvas, the great śrāvakas, bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās.
The devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras,
and mahoragas were all clearly illuminated and appeared distinctly.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke these verses for the sake of all beings:
"I now proclaim the Parittā, Out of compassion for all sentient beings.
This great dhāraṇī Is able to subdue those who are difficult to tame."
All extremely evil and grave offenses— should one merely hear this *Pratītyasamutpāda-hṛdaya-dhāraṇī*, all sins will be extinguished,
all sentient beings will find peace and happiness, and they will be liberated from all diseases.
Out of great compassion for sentient beings, the World-Honored One has therefore taught this for the sake of attaining liberation:
to remain far removed from all evil realms,
even if one enters the palaces of the asuras, yakṣas, or rākṣasas.
Bhūta, nāga, and spirits— into all such palaces one can enter at will; by employing this great vidyā-mantra,
one receives protection in places of battle and danger.
One shall not be thwarted or destroyed by enemies,
nor by various spirits and demons; by the recitation of this dhāraṇī,
all such malevolent beings are utterly annihilated— sajjñonmana, piśāca, kinnara.
Fierce and evil, they suck away vital energy; They constantly harm classes of sentient beings.

May they all be utterly extinguished; Through the merit of the *Prasannatārā* (Suiqiu) mantra, All enemies shall be destroyed, And all malevolent rites of sorcery and incantation shall be neutralized.
Cursing spells shall be ineffective; one shall not suffer the retribution of fixed karma,
nor be struck by toxic poisons, water, fire, blades, thunderbolts,
frost, hail, black winds, or violent rains.
One shall be liberated from all calamities, and all enemies shall be utterly subdued.
If a person maintains this vidyā, or wears it upon their neck or arm, whatever they seek shall be fulfilled;
all their hopes and aspirations shall be realized.
May all attain their heart's desires; may the celestial kings provide protection,
as well as the great nāga kings, the bodhisattvas of great diligence,
the pratyekabuddhas, the śrāvakas, and all the Tathāgatas.
The Greatly Majestic Vidyārājñī shall provide protection for all who uphold the Sādhanā of the Parṇaśabarī Dhāraṇī; likewise,
the Vajra-Guhyapati and the Four World-Protecting Kings shall protect those persons who perform the recitation.
May Śakra and the hosts of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven,
Brahmā and Viṣṇu, as well as Maheśvara,
Kumāra, Mahākāla, and Hārītī, constantly provide protection day and night.
All the hosts of Mother Goddesses, as well as the other hosts of Māras,
the rishis of ascetic power and majesty, and all the deities of secret mantra—
all shall come to protect those who uphold this *Pratisarā*.
The Bodhisattva Mahātejas, the Vidyārājñī Mahākāruṇikā,
the heroic and powerful ones, Māmaki, Bhṛkuṭī,
Tārā, Aṅkuśī, and the other Vajraśṛṅkhalās.
The White-Robed One and the Planet Venus;
the Noble Mahākāla, the Messenger, and the Vajra-Messenger;
the Great Powerful One who wields the Wondrous Lasso and the Vajra-Lasso and holds the Wheel; the Vajra-Garland Great Illuminator.
Amṛtakuṇḍalin, Aparājitā Vidyārājñī,
Kālī Śrīdevī, Mahāpuṇyatejorājā Padmakuṇḍalin, Puṣpadantī, and Maṇicūḍā.
Suvarṇakeśī Piṅgalā, Mahātejaśrī and Vidyutprabhādevī,
Ekaśikharā Mahārākṣasī and Buddhakṣetrasaṃrakṣaṇī, and Kāpālī Prajñādevī.
The Lord of Laṅkā and the many other classes of beings—
all of them provide protection; likewise, Hārītī with her sons,
and the great general Pañcika, who holds the vidyā-mantra in his hand.
Śāṅkhinī, Jambhanī, Dantī, Śrī, and Sarasvatī—
by holding this secret mantra, they will constantly follow one day and night.
If there are women who hold this dhāraṇī, [they shall likewise be protected].
They shall all achieve fulfillment; whether male or female, they shall dwell peacefully within the womb, and the fetus shall grow in safety.
Their birth shall be entirely blissful, all illnesses shall be eliminated, and all transgressions shall be utterly extinguished.
The power of merit is ever complete; grains, wheat, and all treasures shall increase.
Their speech is pleasant to hear, and wherever they go, they receive respect from both men and women.
Pure and able to uphold [the teachings], always harboring a heart of compassion,
they deliver all sentient beings; may they all attain peace and happiness,
and be freed from illness— both the king and his inner court.
All shall give rise to a mind of reverence; auspiciousness will always blaze forth, and the accumulation of merit will increase.
All mantra-dharmas shall be fully accomplished, and one shall enter all maṇḍalas.
Having attained the samaya, as the Tathāgata has truly declared,
evil dreams cannot invade; all sins are completely extinguished,
as are afflictions and enemies, and the calamities of malevolent planets are destroyed.
The Greatly Wise One, Sovereign in Speech, Who can fulfill the wishes and desires of others— Therefore, I shall now speak; may the great assembly listen with full attention.
Namo sarvatathāgatānām | Namo namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ || 2 ||

Jambhanī jambhanī sarvavighnānāṃ bhañjanī bhaginī bhagi bhagi bhagini bhagini bhagavati svāhā. *Note: The transliteration provided in the source text contains several archaic or variant spellings (e.g., *jambhanī*, *bhañjanī*, *bhaginī*, *bhagini*, *bhagavati*).
The translation reflects the standard Sanskrit form of this specific dhāraṇī.* O Jambhanī, O Jambhanī! [Subduer] of all obstacles! O Bhañjanī, O Bhaginī, O Bhagi, O Bhagini, O Bhagini!
O Bhagavatī, svāhā! May there be well-being! (Aṣṭa) *The term "Aṣṭa" at the end indicates that this mantra is to be recited eight times.*

*Dhaṇi hūṃ hūṃ rucaḷe svāhā.* As soon as these four great dhāraṇīs were spoken,
all the Buddhas, the great Bodhisattvas, and the Śrāvakas—
With one voice and in unison, they spoke this Great Parittā Dhāraṇī of the Invincible Mahāvidyārāja Armor Mantra-words,
sealing them with the seal of all Tathāgatas.
This is extremely difficult to hear;
how much more so to write it down, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, and proclaim it for others.
Therefore, one should know that this is a great Buddha-work.
The Tathāgata has most profoundly praised and extolled this name of the Great Amoghapāśa Dhāraṇī;
it is extremely difficult to hear.
It is called the Great Amoghapāśa Dhāraṇī.
It is extremely difficult to hear and exceedingly rare to encounter;
it can exhaust all transgressions.
It possesses great power, valor, and courage, and is endowed with great majesty, virtue, and supernormal might.
It can generate immeasurable merit;
it can destroy all hosts of Māras;
and it can sever all accumulations of habitual tendencies as well as the snares of Māra.
It can eliminate the poisons of others' mantras, as well as rites of suppression, incantations, medicinal spells, methods of mutual hatred, and methods of subjugation.
It can cause sentient beings with malicious minds to give rise to great compassion.
It can protect those who love, delight in, and make offerings to the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and the assembly of noble ones.
It is able to protect those who write down, uphold, recite, and hear the Mahāyāna sūtras,
and it can also fulfill the cultivation of the Buddha-bodhi.
Great Brahmā, hold this Great Parittā Aparājitā Vidyārājñī.
They shall not be discouraged or defeated;
they will receive great offerings everywhere,
just like the Great Teacher, the Buddha, the Honored One among two-legged beings.
How is this known?
It is because this vidyārāja can destroy all māras.
Great Brahmā, in the past there was a Buddha.
He was named Tathāgata Arhat Samyaksaṃbuddha King of Lofty Valor, Radiant with the Blazing Light of the Maṇi-Jewels and a Face of Vast and Broad Smiles.
When he first attained the Way,
he proceeded to the Bodhimaṇḍa, desiring to turn the wheel of Dharma.
All Tathāgatas praised it.
At that time, all Māras, surrounded by immeasurable koṭis of nayutas of followers,
manifested various forms and uttered terrifying sounds.
He manifested various demonic realms and displayed supernatural powers,
raining down all kinds of weapons that came and went from the four directions to create obstacles.
At that time, the Tathāgata King of High Valor, whose face was broad and smiling and who was illuminated by the blazing light of mani-jewels and gold, [responded].
Remaining in silence for a brief moment,
he mentally recited this Great Amoghapāśa Dhāraṇī of the Mahāvidyārājñī Seven times.
As soon as he had finished reciting this dhāraṇī,
In an instant, all the Māras Pāpīyas saw from each and every pore of that Tathāgata emerge immeasurable koṭis of hundreds of thousands of nayutas of Vajra-messengers.
Upon their bodies, those armor-clad beings emitted great radiance;
each held swords, scimitars, battle-axes, nooses, staves, clubs, and tridents,
and each uttered these words:
Those who seize and bind the evil Māras, who crush their malevolent minds;
those who cut short their lives and pulverize all Māras who create obstacles for the Tathāgata—
it is precisely these all-too-hard-to-tame evil Māras [who are thus subdued].
By the great majestic power of the Tathāgata,
a Great Man emerged from within his pores,
causing all these hosts of Māras to faint and fall prostrate upon the ground.
All having lost their inherent nature, supernatural powers, and eloquence, they fled in all directions;
the Tathāgata, with the sword of great compassion,
attained victory over the realm of Māra.
Having attained unsurpassed bodhi,
he immediately turns the wheel of Dharma of all Tathāgatas,
[subduing] all obstructors and vināyakas of all Buddhas.
All the various evil Māras were utterly destroyed;
the Tathāgata then turned the Wheel of Dharma,
transcended the great ocean of birth and death, and reached the other shore.
"O Great Brahmā, this dhāraṇī possesses such great power that it can enable one to attain supernormal powers and reach the further shore;
it is sufficient merely to recollect it."
They shall attain liberation from all perilous places.
With pure intentions, they shall give rise to great compassion for sentient beings with evil minds.
Therefore, Great Brahmā, you should always keep this in mind.
One should practice correct mental attention (*yoniśo-manasikāra*), transcribe it according to the Dharma, and constantly wear and carry it.
Furthermore, Great Brahmā, there was a king in the city of Ujjayanī named Brahmadatta.
There was a certain man who had committed a grave offense against the king.
The king issued a decree that an executioner should lead that criminal to the mountains and take his life.
Having received these instructions, the executioner led the criminal away.
When he reached the mountain cave and was about to kill him with a knife,
that sinner had previously worn this *Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of the Invincible Paritrāṇa* upon his right arm.
The mind further recollects that,
by the power of this great vidyā-mantra,
the blade blazes with light and flames like a mass of fire.
The body was broken into fragments like fine dust.
At that time, the killer, having seen this,
marveled at such an unprecedented occurrence.
He then reported these matters in full to the king.
Upon hearing this, the king became greatly incensed and issued another command,
ordering the executioners to take this criminal and deliver him to the yakṣa cave.
Within that cave dwell many yakṣas who are commanded to devour these criminals;
having received the king’s decree, they immediately lead the criminals away to the yakṣa cave.
As soon as they were cast into the cave,
the hosts of yakṣas, filled with joy and leaping for delight, rushed forward,
desiring to devour the sinners.
Because that sinner possessed the majestic power of the Mahāpratisarā,
at that time the assembly of yakṣas saw a great radiance upon the sinner’s body, blazing and brilliantly shining.
The hosts of yakṣas were all struck with terror and each thought to themselves,
"This fire is coming to burn me."
When that host of yakṣas saw this, they were struck with great terror;
they escorted this sinner to the entrance of their cave, where they circumambulated him and paid him homage.
At that time, the messenger reported all these events to the king, and upon hearing them, the king became even more enraged.
Furthermore, the Emperor commanded the messengers, "Bind that criminal and throw him into the deep river.
Following these instructions, they went and threw him in;
as soon as he entered the river, the water was instantly dried up, becoming like dry land.
At that time, the criminal stood upon the bank;
the ropes with which he was bound snapped one by one.
When the king heard of this matter, he was struck with great astonishment and wonder.
With a joyful smile, he felt great wonder and called out to that sinner,
asking him about his object of perception:
"What do you understand?"
The sinner replied, "Great King, I understand nothing.
Upon my person, I carry only the Great Amoghapāśa Dhāraṇī, the Mantra of the Sovereign King."
The King immediately praised it, saying, "How truly marvelous and extraordinary!
This great vidyā-mantra is subtle and wondrous, capable of crushing the punishment of death.
He then spoke a verse:
The Great Mantra is most subtle and wondrous, Able to destroy the punishments of death.
Sustained by the empowerment of all Buddhas, It rescues and delivers all sentient beings.
It can liberate them from the disease of suffering; The Great Mantra possesses great majestic power.
One can escape untimely death; this was taught by the Great Compassionate Honored One.
It can halt great diseases and swiftly lead to the realization of Great Bodhi.
At that time, the king rejoiced and leaped for joy.
He immediately took that *pratisarā* [amulet] and made offerings and prostrations to it.
He then tied a silk scarf around the head of the criminal and conferred upon him the consecration (*abhiṣeka*) and title of Lord of the City, according to the custom of the five regions of India.
When conferring official honors, all have silk and cloth tied around their heads;
only after the consecration (abhiṣeka) is the office bestowed. Thus it is, Mahābrahmā, with this Great Dhāraṇī of the Invincible Great Paritrāṇā.
If anyone wears it, they will receive great offerings in all places;
even those sentient beings with unruly and evil minds will all give rise to compassion and submit to them in harmony.
Therefore, one should always wear and carry this great dhāraṇī.
Furthermore, Mahābrahmā, if one wishes to wear this dhāraṇī,
one should select an auspicious day, an auspicious lunar mansion, and a propitious time.
Having written down this dhāraṇī according to the ritual,
the Great Brahmā King, upon hearing these words,
was filled with immense joy.
Touching the ground with his five limbs, he prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and addressed the Buddha, saying: "By what method should this Great Parittā Aparājita Dhāraṇī be written?"
At that time, the Tathāgata spoke these verses, addressing Mahābrahmā:
"Mahābrahmā, you should know: I shall now speak for your sake."
Out of compassion for all sentient beings, may they attain great peace and happiness,
be freed from oppressive karma, and be liberated from all diseases;
may pregnant women be safe, and may sentient beings be rid of poverty.
All karmic obscurations shall be completely eliminated. During an auspicious lunar mansion,
when the Puṣya constellation is in conjunction, one should observe the fast and precepts and make offerings to the Buddhas, generating the great bodhicitta.
Again, generate a mind of compassion and arouse a heart of great loving-kindness;
thinking of the benefit of others, bathe all classes of sentient beings with this fragrant water of nāga-urine, musk, and sandalwood.
Donning new and clean garments, one should further fumigate with incense;
using *gomaya* [cow dung], one should smear a small maṇḍala.
One should take five "excellent" vases (*bhadraghaṭa*), all filled to the brim with scented water.
Intersperse various flowers and fruits, placing them at the four corners of the maṇḍala;
set the remainder in the center of the maṇḍala.
One should offer flower garlands, burning incense, and exquisite unguents, as well as incense of the five flavors.
Burn sandalwood, *saptaparṇa*, ghee, incense, and rock honey blended together;
at all times, offer various exquisite flowers, fruits, and seeds as offerings.
Using scented ointments for adornment, with ghee, honey, and curdled milk,
along with parched grain and milk-rice; these should be placed in full offering vessels,
all of which are auspicious according to their measure, contained within ceramic or earthenware bowls.
Four square vessels filled with incense; stakes of khadira wood are driven into the four corners of the maṇḍala;
five-colored threads are wound around the four corners on the exterior of the maṇḍala.
By means of this rite, Mahābrahmā [attains success].
One who seeks siddhi should consume the three white foods and write this [mantra] according to the petitioner's request;
one should sit within the maṇḍala upon a pure mat of kuśa grass and transcribe it according to the ritual rules.
Whether on plain silk or brocade, or written upon birch bark,
leaves, or other materials— those women who seek offspring should transcribe this dhāraṇī using ox-gall (gorocana).
In the center, paint the Youth (Kumāra), his body adorned with jeweled necklaces;
holding a full alms-bowl filled with precious gems in his left hand,
he sits upon a lotus flower that is in full bloom.
Furthermore, in the western corner, one should paint four precious mountains;
these mountains are adorned with gold and jewels. One should diligently paint them in this way, for it can bring peace and security to the womb for a man seeking a son.
One should employ saffron for writing;
all that is sought shall be fully accomplished.
On the four sides of the mantra, one should draw various mudrās, and furthermore, draw lotuses.
There may be two, three, four, or even five lotus flowers, all of which are in full bloom;
each has eight petals, complete with filaments and anthers, and their stalks are bound with silk.
Upon each flower, one should paint a trident.
Furthermore, silk streamers are tied to the halberd;
likewise, the battle-axe is also depicted upon a lotus flower.
Moreover, upon a white lotus flower, a sword should be painted; it is also situated upon a lotus flower.
And they are drawn upon a conch shell;
all the lotuses thus depicted are within a jeweled pond. If a man wears it, one should not depict a youth;
rather, one should depict the forms of devas and humans.
Adorned with various jewels, if a king were to wear it,
one should paint [the image] therein; furthermore, one should paint the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara and various mudrās on its four sides.
If it is for a bhikṣu, one should depict him holding a vajra;
with his right hand he grasps a vajra, and his left fist has its index finger raised, pointing toward those who are difficult to tame.
Furthermore, [this should be done] at the four corners.
One should depict the Four Heavenly Kings;
if a Brahmin wears [the thread], one should depict Īśāna;
if a Kṣatriya wears it, one should depict Maheśvara; and if a Vaiśya wears it...
If it is for Śakra, the Lord of Devas, one should paint him;
or if it is Vaiśravaṇa, he should likewise be painted. If it is for a Śūdra, one should paint Nārāyaṇa;
for a young boy or girl, one should paint Pārvatī.
The woman of the blue-clad [deity] should be painted;
the woman of the white-clad Raudrā should be painted.
The woman of the deity named Yaśasvinī should be painted if she is full and well-nourished; one should paint that Ratnacūḍa.
If it is a slender woman, one should paint the yakṣa Pūrṇabhadra;
if she is pregnant, one should paint Mahākāla or Brahmā.
Such are the types of human beings [to be depicted].
One should paint the deity venerated in each respective manuscript and transcribe it according to the ritual rules;
by constantly wearing it upon one's person, all that is sought will be fulfilled as desired.
One should fashion a lotus flower from gold or copper and place a precious gem upon it.
In the shape of a wish-fulfilling flame, it is placed atop a banner or pinnacle;
within this jewel, one installs the Great Parittā (Mahāpratisarā),
and within that Parittā, one should draw the lord of the city.
If this *Sūramgama* shrine is established within one's own residence,
one should paint the principal deity at its center; on all four sides of the *Sūramgama*,
one should draw lotuses surrounding it, and upon the pericarp and filaments of the flowers—
One should depict a noose, a vajra, a wheel,
a staff, and a śakti; these various mudrās should each rest upon a lotus,
with silken banners suspended above them.
One should make offerings in accordance with the Dharma; by this, according to one's prayers,
the Buddha-field shall protect the kingdom, cities, and towns, as well as the family,
so that all calamities are utterly extinguished, including pestilence and all manner of diseases.
Famine shall not prevail, and foreign enemies shall not invade;
the land shall be peaceful and happy. When encountering extreme drought or persistent rain, one should paint a nine-headed dragon.
Upon its head is a jewel from which flames stream forth;
it should be placed upon the heart of the nāga.
On the four sides of the nāga’s body, draw a vajra and write this Great Parittā (Mahāpratisarā).
Placed within a casket, or likewise installed atop a banner or stupa,
it shall cause sweet rain to fall at the proper time, and when rain is excessive, it will immediately clear the skies.
Whether leading a caravan of people on land or by water, the merchant lord remains steadfast.
For those merchants who carry it, one should paint the form of the caravan leader as previously described and install it upon the stūpa;
they will escape robbers and all fears and reach the further shore. Therefore, one should be diligent.
By wearing, carrying, and reciting this, auspiciousness shall arise and all sins be extinguished.
If there is one who performs the recitation, they should paint their own tutelary deity,
as well as the sun, the moon, Mars, Mercury, and Jupiter.
Venus and Saturn, comets and Rāhu— through these and other such nine grahas,
whatever calamities and misfortunes are caused by their transgressing and oppressing one’s natal asterism, all shall be completely liberated.
Or there may be a stone-woman, or one of the *śaṇḍha* or *paṇḍaka* types;
even such persons as these, by wearing the Mahāpratisarā,
can yet have offspring— if those of such a kind wear it.
One should paint the nine planetary deities and the twenty-eight lunar mansions;

within the celestial sphere, one should depict those figures. Whatever is sought shall be fulfilled according to one's wishes, just as the World-Honored One has taught, and one shall attain the most supreme state.
In this life and in future lives, one shall always obtain supreme happiness;
one will be born at will in the celestial palace of the Thirty-three Gods,
or in the delightful land of Jambudvīpa within the most eminent families.
One shall be born into such a lineage— whether among the Kṣatriyas, the gods,
or the families of Brāhmaṇas— by wearing this Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra;
thus one attains these most excellent states through writing, upholding, and reciting it.
If one wears this according to the Dharma, one shall go to the Land of Bliss and be born transformed within a lotus; there is no doubt or hesitation regarding this,
for all Tathāgatas praise and proclaim these merits.
Praising them cannot exhaust their virtues; they close the gates of hell and open the paths to the celestial realms.
They bring about the complete accomplishment of peace and happiness, and all their wisdom is perfected—such are the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
He constantly comforts those people, Their bodies always experience happiness;
Brave and possessing great strength, The Tathāgata speaks these truthful words:
They shall obtain the rank of a Wheel-Turning King, Comforting the multitudes of humans and devas.
Those with fearful and evil minds shall, by practicing this dhāraṇī,
attain its power before long; they will not be harmed by blades,
nor by poisons, fire, or water— none of these shall be able to injure them.
Neither untimely death nor premature demise— may all such evils be kept far away.
Whether seen, heard, or touched by the body,
may the terrors of malevolent spirits and strife be extinguished at all times and in all places.
Malevolent insects and venomous snakes are all completely liberated from confinement;
various minor and major illnesses are entirely extinguished by practicing this vidyā-mantra,
[bringing peace] to the hosts of Māras.
Unimpeded and attaining thorough penetration, One is able to receive great offerings in all places;
Among humans, one receives the most supreme protection while practicing the mantra.
Chapter Two: The Chapter on the Practice of the Bodhisattva’s Great Protective Mahāvidyārājñī Dhāraṇī, the *Pratisarā*. At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Mahābrahmā, speaking in verse:
I shall now proclaim for the practitioners of vidyādhara,
the ritual procedure for bestowing protection; through this safeguarding out of compassion for all sentient beings,
they shall attain great accomplishment.
In whatever place one dwells, by using this to perform empowerment,
one attains freedom from obstacles; with a resolute mind free from doubt,
fear, and affliction, all malevolent spirits are extinguished.
In accordance with the lunar mansions and planets, it can sever the fetters of karma;
evil food, evil leaping, and the loathing of written spells are all utterly extinguished,
and all enemies are eliminated so that one is not oppressed or harmed.
Evil glares and suppressive incantations, spells with medicinal herbs and poisonous charms—
whether directed at enemies in treacherous places or in situations of great terror against hostile foes—
all these are entirely dissolved through the power of Mahāpratisarā.
All Buddhas provide protection; all Bodhisattvas of Universal Wisdom bestow their grace.
Pratyekabuddhas and Śrāvakas, as well as various other classes of beings—the great and majestic devas and nāgas—[all likewise protect].
All shall provide protection for those who recite this secret mantra;
by merely hearing it, the most supreme and honored Vidyārāja becomes fearless in all places— thus spoke the Muni.
Bad dreams and mental distress, And most terrible afflictions;
when diseases envelop the body, Such as emaciation that wastes away the flesh and bones,
And various other manifold ailments, Including carbuncles and all manner of toxic swellings.
Evil possession and calamities, and the biting and devouring of sentient beings—
those acts done for the purpose of harming sentient beings— are all utterly extinguished;
through the protection of this great mantra, all such great harms and extreme terrors are completely eliminated.
Through this empowerment of light, those who are destined for death shall attain liberation;
even if bound by black cords and led to the palace of the Lord of Death,
their lifespan shall be doubled, because they wear this great protection written upon them.
If there is one whose lifespan is exhausted and who is destined to die after seven days,
merely by writing this mantra and wearing it,
or by merely hearing it, and by consecrating it according to the ritual, there shall be unsurpassed great protection.
Attaining peace and security everywhere, they enjoy bliss according to their wishes;
sixty-eight koṭis and one hundred nayutas of the thirty-three devas assist Śakra.
May the Four Great World-Protecting Kings come to guard this person, following them to provide protection;
may the powerful Vajrapāṇi and the assembly of a hundred vidyā families constantly protect that person.
The Sun God and the Moon God, Brahmā and Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, and the Yāma gods;
Ratnapāla, Baladeva, Pūrṇabhadra, and Mahāvīra; Hārītī and her sons.
Pañcāla and Pañcikā; the Auspicious Great Vidyārājñī, Sovereign of the Kumāras;
Sarasvatī, the Goddess of Wisdom and Eloquence;
Śakunī and Puṣpadantī; Ekajaṭī of Great Majesty.
Thus, this great yakṣa shall always provide protection;
may he protect the children born of Śilāvatī,
causing their gestation to flourish and constantly guarding that person for as long as life endures.
The man shall always be victorious in places of fear and battle;
by this, all his wishes are fulfilled. All sins are utterly extinguished through reliance on the devas with pure faith and by writing down this great mantra.
The Buddhas always observe him; for that Bodhisattva of great majesty, his fame shall increase, as shall his merit and lifespan.
His wealth and grain will all be abundant, and he shall obtain everything without doubt.
Whether asleep or awake, one shall find complete peace and happiness;
neither enemies nor malevolent spirits shall be able to cause harm.
In times of battle, one shall always achieve victory.
When practicing mantras, this protection is the most supreme;
for those who practice vidyās with ease, they shall encounter no obstacles,
and all the teachings of the secret mantras shall be fully accomplished.
One enters all maṇḍalas and swiftly accomplishes the samaya;
even unto future lives, all Buddhas entrust their secrets to one who maintains this great protection, and all auspiciousness shall be fulfilled.
All intentions will be fully accomplished; by merely writing this vidyā, all happiness and prosperity will arise.
One will live in peace and, upon passing away, will certainly be reborn in a happy realm.
If one desires to be born in the Land of Utmost Bliss, [one should do so].
Whoever wears this vidyārāja will certainly be free from doubt;
in disputes, litigation, battlefields, and amidst great terrors,
all fears shall be far removed, just as the Buddha has truly spoken.
They constantly attain the knowledge of past lives, And in every birth they are free from doubt.
All kings rejoice, As do their inner courts and retinues, who all constantly show them respect;
They always associate with virtuous people.
May they all give rise to compassion for both humans and devas,
and grant them protection; may this Great Protective Accomplishment Vidyā, spoken by the Samyaksaṃbuddha, provide constant guardianship day and night.

RAṆI MĀRA MĀRA JAYA VINAYE HŪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ. The Buddha said to Mahābrahmā:
If there is anyone who, by means of the mantra-words of the Tathāgata’s Body-Vidyā-dhāraṇī,
performs empowerment, rescue, gathering, and protection,
they will be able to perform rites for the pacification of calamities and the creation of auspiciousness.
It wards off punishments and effects great protection.
If a person’s lifespan is about to end,
by reciting this mantra, they shall again obtain the extension of life and increased longevity.
For a long time they shall remain alive, constantly attaining peace and happiness, and obtaining great mindfulness and retention.
If one merely recites the mantra while empowering it with the vajra,
those who suffer from untimely death or grave illnesses shall be cured.
All shall attain liberation.
All diseases shall be eradicated.
Those who have suffered from chronic illness should recite this mantra.
By consecrating the corner of one's *kāṣāya* robe and waving it over that patient, the illness is immediately cured.
Those who recite and maintain this daily shall attain great wisdom, power, great diligence, and the accomplishment of eloquence.
All karmic retributions for sinful obstructions shall be entirely extinguished.
All Buddhas and Bodhisattvas,
as well as devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and others [will likewise witness this].
For those who uphold this dhāraṇī,
it shall cause their vital essence to enter their bodies, increasing their power;
they shall always experience joy in both body and mind.
Mahābrahmā, if even those as lowly as animals or birds should hear this Great Vidyārāja, the Great Protective Dhāraṇī,
they shall all never again regress from unsurpassed bodhi.
How much more so for those with pure faith— sons and daughters of good family,
bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas and upāsikās,
kings, princes, brahmins, kṣatriyas, and all other such classes.
Upon hearing this Great Dhāraṇī of the Great Amoghapāśa for Universal Protection,
having heard it, one should with a profound mind of pure faith and reverence copy, read, and recite it;
and with a heart of earnest devotion, one should practice its cultivation.
He extensively expounds and disseminates it for others.
Great Brahmā is entirely free from the eight kinds of wrong livelihood;
thus, no disease arises within his body.
They shall not be harmed by the poisons of fire, weapons, or staves, nor by malevolent spells, sorcery, curses,
or any evil medicinal rites. They shall not suffer from bodily pain,
headaches, or various types of malaria— whether occurring once, twice, thrice, four times, or even up to seven days.
Furthermore, they will not be afflicted by epilepsy or other such maladies;
they shall sleep with right mindfulness and awaken with right mindfulness,
realizing great nirvana.
In this present life, one attains great wealth, nobility, and mastery.
In whatever place one is born, one will always possess the recollection of past lives.
All humans and devas will love and respect them, and their physical appearance and deportment will be upright and handsome.
All beings in the hells, hungry ghosts, and the animal realm attained liberation.
It was as if the solar disc illuminated all sentient beings with its radiance,
and like the lunar disc drenching the bodies of all sentient beings with nectar.
He brings joy to those people;
through the nectar of the Dharma, he enters the mental continuums of all sentient beings,
causing them all to be moistened and filled with gladness.
All evil yakṣas, rākṣasas,
bhūtas, and piśācas.
Piśācas, epileptic spirits, ḍākinīs,
and various malevolent spirits.
The vināyakas and others shall all be unable to harass or afflict [this person] by the power of this Great Parittā, the Great Protection;
even if they should approach and draw near.
By recollecting this Great Dhāraṇī Queen,
all those of malicious intent will give rise to joy toward the person who maintains the recitation.
Having received these instructions, they departed.
By the power of this Great Parittā, the Great Dhāraṇī Queen,
there shall ultimately be no fear of enemies or adversaries.
These various enemies will be unable to assail or overcome them.
Or, if there should be someone who [relies upon this] in the presence of kings, ministers, brahmins, or householders.
If one who has committed a transgression or offense deserving of death by execution should,
at the moment of facing the blade of a sword at the site of the execution,
merely bring this Great Protective Vidyārāja to mind.
The blades were shattered into fragments like fine dust;
at that moment, the person attained the realization of the equality of all phenomena.
One attains great power of mindfulness.
At that time, the Tathāgata spoke these verses:
"This great protection and empowerment is pure and extinguishes all sins."
It can produce the auspiciousness of wisdom, increase all merits,
fulfill all blessings, and eliminate inauspiciousness;
it enables one to see wondrous and beautiful dreams and purify all evil dreams.
This great vidyā is a great protection;
it protects men and women in wildernesses and perilous fears.
One attains liberation in an instant and obtains all desired wishes, as taught by the Perfectly Awakened One.
If one loses the way while traveling, by recollecting this Great Vidyārāja,
one will swiftly regain the correct path. Having obtained excellent food and drink,
through the actions of body, speech, and mind, whatever sins were previously committed—
Whatever unwholesome karma has been committed, by merely recollecting this vidyā,
it shall all be completely extinguished; whether by writing it down,
receiving and upholding it, reciting and chanting it, or explaining it to others.
One thoroughly penetrates all phenomena; thus attaining the flavor of the Dharma, all transgressions are immediately extinguished.
Whatever matters the mind desires and seeks shall all be accomplished.
Amidst all fears of death, [one is secure].
All shall be obtained and protected from kings, officials, water, fire,
frost, hail, and bandits; from the perils of battle, litigation,
and beasts with sharp teeth and claws— all such things shall be entirely dissolved away.
By reciting it one hundred thousand times, this vidyā is swiftly accomplished;
so have all the Buddhas declared. By reciting it with devotion, one brings joy to [the deity], fulfills the provisions for enlightenment, and [attains mastery] in every place where one dwells.
If one employs this great vidyā-mantra to perform consecrations and to carry out various activities,
the welfare of oneself and others will be spontaneously accomplished;
there is no doubt that it provides great protection.
Mahābrahmā, you should know: I shall now further proclaim that for one who is gravely ill,
one should construct a square mandala using cow dung mixed with clay, and draw it with five-colored powders.
Then one should construct a maṇḍala; the wise person, following the ritual manual, places four vases at the four corners.
Upon the altar, one should scatter various flowers, burn excellent incense, and offer various kinds of food and drink.
Seeing this, people are moved to pure faith;
thus one should offer incense and flowers according to the ritual.
Insert four arrows at the four corners and bind them with five-colored threads, then cause the patient to bathe.
Wearing pure garments and with his entire body anointed with fragrant unguents,
he is led to the center of the maṇḍala and sits facing the east.
At that time, the vidyādhara first recites this great mantra:
Recite this seven times to empower oneself;
then recite it twenty-one times to empower the patient.
By reciting this great protection, all illnesses shall be pacified and eliminated.
Then take one water flask, fill it with fragrant flowers and food, and perform the consecration seven times. Cast it far away toward the east;
next, take the flask from the south, [filling it] with flowers, incense, and food according to the instructions.
Recite as before seven times and cast [the offering] far away toward the south.
Next, use the western flask; with flowers, incense, and food and drink, perform the empowerment ritual as previously described. Do the same for the northern direction.
At that time, the practitioner, looking upward toward the zenith,
should recite this vidyā once. Having thus performed the supreme empowerment of Mahābrahmā, all sufferings are entirely eliminated.
Such is this empowerment-dharma taught by the Lion of the Śākyas;
among all dharmas, there is none that can compare with it.
It is the supreme protection within the three realms; those who possess it shall not suffer untimely death.
Without old age and without illness, free from the suffering of separation from those one hates—
if one can contemplate according to the principle, the mind will be free from sorrow and suffering,
and free from the suffering of the aggregate of sensation; thus shall the hosts of Māra offer worship.
The Dharma King of Yama, having been served with reverence, told that vidyādhara:
"By means of this great mantra, go quickly to the celestial realms;
thus, the hells shall be entirely emptied."
Then, riding upon a wondrous celestial palace, endowed with majesty, one shall reach the heavens;
all humans and devas, as well as the hosts of yakṣas and rākṣasas,
will all offer worship, and one shall constantly obtain such merit.
Therefore, one should always uphold [this teaching]:
the secret yakṣa general Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva, Śacī the consort of Indra,
the host of Hārītī mothers, and the yakṣa Pañcika.
The World-Protectors of great majesty, the sun, moon, and constellations,
the fierce and malevolent planetary deities, all the great nāga kings,
the devas along with the hosts of sages, the asuras, and the nāgas.
The garuḍas, gandharvas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas—
by writing down this vidyā and constantly reciting it according to the dharma,
they shall always follow one and obtain great prosperity.
At that time, when the World-Honored One had finished speaking this sutra,
the assembly of great bodhisattvas and great śrāvakas,
as well as the Brahma Heaven King, all the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, gandharvas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so forth, [all rejoiced].
All were greatly rejoiced, and having faith and acceptance, they practiced accordingly.
May those who have come to hear the Dharma— the devas, asuras, yakṣas, and others—
protect the Buddha-dharma with a sincere heart so that it may endure long, and may each of them diligently carry out the teachings of the World-Honored One.
All you disciples who have come here, whether dwelling upon the earth or abiding in the sky,
may you always give rise to a heart of compassion for the world of humans; may you dwell in accordance with the Dharma throughout day and night,
and may all worlds be forever peaceful and secure, benefiting all living beings through boundless merit and wisdom.
May all karmic offenses be completely eliminated; May one remain far removed from all suffering and enter parinirvāṇa.

Constantly anointing the body with the fragrance of ethical discipline, Always wearing the robes of meditative concentration to sustain the self, Adorned everywhere with the exquisite flowers of bodhi— Wherever one dwells, may there always be peace and joy.

Vajra-pāṇi-mahā-krodha-rāja-sarva-duṣṭa-nivāraṇa-hūṃ-phat.

The King of High and Valiant Radiance, who illuminates the city of the hell realms with the body of the Tathāgatagarbha—perfected in the *pāramitās* of meditative concentration, wisdom, skillful means, vows, power, and knowledge; possessing the five eyes and the accomplishment of the Buddha-dharma; adorned on all limbs with the secondary marks (*anuvyañjana*) such as the tree of the celestial palace; and who utters the roar of the fierce lion.
